name: W S DARLEY & CO
brief_text:
Three detectors fired for W S Darley & Co. The Benford test found significant deviation in leading-digit frequencies across 4,213 transactions, with a p-value near zero indicating the observed distribution departs substantially from expected natural patterns. The modification-growth detector identified one contract (SPE8EJ21D0025) whose modifications grew at a ratio of 14,372, roughly 28 times faster than the NAICS peer average of 519, yielding a z-score of 5.92. The Isolation Forest algorithm flagged the entity as a multivariate outlier with a score of 0.95, driven primarily by concentration with a single awarding agency despite substantial lifetime volume.

The entity has obligated $2.79 billion across 4,213 awards, all from the Department of Defense. The Benford leading-digit distribution shows observed frequencies of 25% for digit 1 versus the expected 30%, and 17% for digit 3 versus expected 12%, with a Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic of 0.057. The worst-performing contract modification ratio of 14,372 compares to a NAICS average of 519. The isolation score reflects that all awards come from one agency, though the entity operates across 14 NAICS codes and maintains a 99.7% competition ratio.

These statistical anomalies warrant scrutiny but do not confirm fraud. Benford deviations can arise from legitimate business practices, contract structures, or rounding conventions in a large, specialized defense supplier. The extreme modification growth on a single contract may reflect legitimate scope expansion or a data artifact. The single-agency concentration is expected for a dedicated defense contractor. The peer group for "All Other Miscellaneous Manufacturing" is broad and may not capture industry-specific norms for this supplier.
